title: UnreliableRemoteEvent
summary: The lightweight sibling of RemoteEvent: identical API (FireServer/FireClient/FireAllClients, OnServerEvent/OnClientEvent) but messages are NOT guaranteed to arrive or to arrive in order — in exchange for lower overhead. Ideal for frequent, replaceable state updates.

verification.notes: Introduced in 2022. Behavior summary checked against the class reference and Roblox networking guidance.

methods.name: FireServer
methods.description: Client only. Sends an unreliable message to the server. Same argument rules as RemoteEvent.

methods.name: FireClient
methods.description: Server only. Sends an unreliable message to one player.

methods.name: FireAllClients
methods.description: Server only. Broadcasts an unreliable message to all players.

events.name: OnServerEvent
events.description: Server only. Fires for each message that DOES arrive from a client. The Player is always the first parameter, exactly like RemoteEvent.

events.name: OnClientEvent
events.description: Client only. Fires for each message that DOES arrive from the server.

details.heading: Reliability behavior
details.body: Unlike RemoteEvent, messages are sent without retransmission: **a message may be dropped entirely under network load**. There is no delivery confirmation. Roblox throttles unreliable sends, so bursts beyond what the network can carry are dropped rather than queued.

details.heading: Ordering behavior
details.body: No ordering guarantee: message 3 can arrive before message 2 (or message 2 may never come). Consumers must treat each message as standalone — typically by using timestamps/sequence numbers or simply by always applying the newest data.

details.heading: Argument rules
details.body: Same serialization rules and limits as RemoteEvent (tables deep-copied, no functions/threads, size limits apply).

details.heading: Cost
details.body: Cheaper than reliable remotes because the engine skips retransmission bookkeeping and buffering — the whole point is to avoid spending bandwidth/CPU on data that will be stale in a frame anyway.

explanation.whatItIs: A RemoteEvent that trades delivery guarantees for efficiency. Same API, same usage pattern — but the network is allowed to drop messages when it's congested, and it won't preserve order.
explanation.whyItExists: Reliable, ordered delivery has a cost: retransmissions and buffering. For data that's refreshed constantly (a position sent 20 times a second), losing one update doesn't matter — the next one replaces it. Paying the reliability tax there is pure waste.
whenToUse: High-frequency state snapshots: custom character/camera positions, aiming data, cosmetic trails
Telemetry and metrics (ping samples, FPS reports) where losing a sample is harmless
Rapidly-changing indicators: typing status, live minimap pings, health-over-head updates
Any case where NEW data fully replaces OLD data
whenNotToUse: One-shot important events: purchases, chat messages, damage, 'player pressed jump' — anything where a lost message changes gameplay
Ordered sequences that must not be rearranged (level progression, story beats)
Anything where the receiver needs to ACK or respond — use RemoteFunction
As a 'faster RemoteEvent' for everything — dropping important messages creates mysterious bugs
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
RemoteEvent           = certified mail     (tracked, ordered, resends if lost)
UnreliableRemoteEvent = tossing notes      (fast; wind may take some; order varies)

Send 1 → 2 → 3
Reliable:    arrives 1, 2, 3        (all, in order)
Unreliable:  maybe 1, 3, 2 — or just 3
```
Design consumers around 'latest message wins'.
tips: Send the FULL current state each time, not deltas — receivers can always recover from a dropped message
Throttle your send rate (e.g. coalesce to once per Heartbeat) instead of firing per input
Include a timestamp or counter if the receiver needs to discard stale messages
Test with simulated bad network conditions before shipping an unreliable-heavy design
commonMistakes: Using it for critical one-time events and seeing them 'randomly' not happen
Sending deltas ('x += 5') — a dropped message permanently desyncs the value
Assuming order: applying message 2 after message 3 corrupts sequences
Expecting the API to warn you about drops — silence is the only signal

examples.title: Throttled position telemetry (the right way)
examples.description: Send full snapshots at a capped rate from Heartbeat, not per physics step.
examples.code:
-- == LocalScript ==
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local posRemote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("CustomPosition")

local player = game.Players.LocalPlayer
local lastSent = 0

RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
    local now = os.clock()
    if now - lastSent < 0.1 then return end   -- ~10 updates/second max
    lastSent = now

    local root = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
    if not root then return end

    -- FULL state + timestamp: dropped messages never corrupt anything
    posRemote:FireServer(root.Position, now)
end)

-- == Script (server) ==
posRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, position, timestamp)
    if typeof(position) ~= "Vector3" or typeof(timestamp) ~= "number" then return end
    player:SetAttribute("ReportedPosition", position)
    -- (a real anti-cheat would sanity-check distance from server truth)
end)
examples.whyItWorks: Every message is a complete, timestamped snapshot. If the network drops half of them, the receiver simply applies the newest one that arrives — no gaps, no drift.
examples.commonMistake: Sending `root.Position` 60+ times a second unthrottled. Unreliable sends are throttled anyway; coalescing keeps bandwidth sane.

examples.title: Why NOT: a one-shot event over unreliable
examples.code:
-- ❌ BAD: critical event on an unreliable remote
chatRemote:FireServer("Hello everyone!")   -- may simply never arrive

-- ✅ GOOD: reliable RemoteEvent for chat, damage, purchases
chatRemote:FireServer("Hello everyone!")    -- RemoteEvent: guaranteed delivery
examples.commonMistake: Players report 'my chat messages sometimes don't send'. Cause: an UnreliableRemoteEvent carrying one-shot events.
